# Windows installation engine

The installation engine stages verified Windows directory packages and publishes an active release record. A runnable unsigned setup executable composes payload extraction, kit verification, progress and cancellation. Stable launch, shortcuts, uninstall registration and clean-machine acceptance remain delivery gates.

`createWindowsInstallation()` from `scripts/windows-installation.mjs` exposes two host-only operations:

- `install({ bundle, installRoot, signal?, onProgress? })` verifies the complete source package with the production bundle verifier, copies its exact inventory into a fresh release directory, verifies the copy, then publishes `installation.json` through a single file replacement.
- `status(installRoot)` reads bounded installation metadata. Its `integrityVerified: false` explicitly distinguishes a record observation from a verified executable.

The installer host chooses the program directory. The engine requires its parent to exist and admits only an empty new directory or a valid existing Arcane installation. App profiles and projects remain separate. Updates retain previous releases and unrelated files. Failed candidates remain available for inspection and are never automatically adopted or removed.

On Windows, admission reserves the complete release and bundled runtime path below 260 characters. This check happens before verification or target mutation: copying files successfully alone cannot establish that Windows can start a child from that directory. See Microsoft's [current-directory restriction](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-setcurrentdirectory). No machine path policy is changed.

An exclusive operation lock fences concurrent installers. Its identity and contents are checked throughout the operation. Changed records, locks, copied files, directories, extra entries, links and junctions refuse publication. The final tree must match the verified inventory, including when reactivating a retained release. Filesystem checks use cooperative ownership and identity; operating-system isolation remains separate.

An optional `AbortSignal` cancels before publication, retaining the previous selection and the candidate. Cancellation after completed publication still reports the installed release. The trusted, synchronous `onProgress` observer returns `undefined` and receives frozen phase/file/byte counters. It supplies presentation metadata rather than installation authority.

Failures preserve the primary cause and report `published: false`, `true` or `null` for retained selection, completed publication or unconfirmed publication. Lock-cleanup failures are retained separately. There is no automatic retry, stale-lock takeover, program launch, shortcut creation, registry write or profile deletion. Retention is bounded to 32 recorded releases; removal and interrupted-install recovery need their own explicit host workflow.

Focused tests use actual temporary filesystems with a labelled small-inventory verifier. Full package acceptance uses the production verifier and separately records the engine source hash and bundle manifest. Neither fixture coverage nor package copying establishes a complete installer or an authenticated customer task.

`createWindowsSetupPayload()` from `scripts/windows-setup-payload.mjs` streams a deterministic stored ZIP containing the verified bundle and a fixed five-module installation kit. The kit manifest independently pins the bundle manifest, bundled Node and each kit file; the returned receipt also pins the entire payload and kit manifest. Changed inputs or replaced outputs refuse acceptance and retain the candidate. The actual C# reader extracts the writer's data-descriptor format in a separate console fixture.

`KitVerifier.Verify(stage, expectedKitManifestSha256)` supplies the separate check before executing extracted code. It admits exactly the fixed installation modules, checks their hashes and sizes, checks the bundled Node hash and x64 PE header, and binds the bundle manifest to its approved hash. Unexpected kit entries and redirected ancestors refuse admission. Native C# harness tests use synthetic runtimes without executing them. These filesystem checks assume cooperative ownership; they do not isolate the installer from other processes running as the same user.

The signed installation-engine snapshot `b898ff2c9749e13a285f9228370bed74acd7917e` installed the existing application package from `186787684c1b964ea03c02d10c00c474889dcb5a` into a fresh owned temporary directory. Production verification covered all 4,174 payload files and the manifest before and after copying; activation took 67,955 ms and retained the separate profile fixture. The installed executable then passed all 32 startup, renderer, bundled MCP and shutdown checks in 32,555 ms. Its screenshot was reviewed. The application manifest remains `d4f015fd7275886ced9f784c6ce4efffc2d812efaec54eb8fe985ac810e422ae`; later application changes are excluded. No setup GUI, shortcuts, registration, application signature, provider inference or Studio operation was involved.

## Setup executable

On Windows x64, build setup from an existing verified bundle and an existing output directory:

```powershell
npm run package:setup -- --bundle "C:\ArcaneBuild\Bundle" --output-parent "C:\ArcaneBuild\Output"
```

The build uses the in-box .NET Framework compiler and emits a unique directory containing `Arcane-Setup.exe`, its payload and a build receipt. The receipt pins native sources, build helpers, icon, compiler and kit files. Payload and kit-manifest hashes are compiled into the executable; assembly rechecks every copied input. The build never launches setup. Setup runs as the current user and selects `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Arcane` after the human clicks Install. Bundled Node supplies installation execution; the installed customer needs no separate Node or npm installation. Native components require .NET Framework 4.7.2 or later; clean-machine runtime acceptance remains open.

The [internal protocol](WINDOWS_INSTALLER_PROTOCOL.md) carries bounded progress and exactly one terminal result. Closing during work requests cancellation and waits for the actual outcome. The UI distinguishes unchanged selection, completed publication and unconfirmed state. It neither retries automatically nor kills active installation work.

Temporary-stage selection expands existing short path aliases and reserves the complete payload path budget. Successful extraction records each created file's bytes, hash and handle identity, and each directory's identity. After a confirmed outcome, cleanup consumes that receipt once and deletes only unchanged owned files through verified handles and owned empty directories. Added, edited, replaced, hardlinked or redirected entries remain. Unconfirmed work, extraction/kit failures and cleanup failures retain their files and report retention without changing the installation result.

The integrated native components were compiled with the actual setup sources and exercised through a separate acceptance harness against the real appended payload. They installed the existing application bundle through its extracted, verified Node and CLI, acknowledged the selected release, then removed all 4,181 extracted files and 655 directories. The active record matched the result, the stage was absent afterward, and the separate profile fixture was unchanged. All 16 build-source hashes matched the executable's receipt. Idle native controls were rendered and reviewed without input. This proves component composition with an owned temporary target; the production GUI was not clicked, the fixed user Programs target was not used, and neither registration nor shortcuts were created. This candidate still contains application source `186787684c1b964ea03c02d10c00c474889dcb5a`; integration of a newer application rebuild, signed distribution and complete customer acceptance remain separate gates.

## Stable launcher component

`InstalledLauncher` reads the strict active-release record, checks the selected manifest and verifies the size, hash and x64 PE identity of the executable it starts. It keeps deny-write handles through one direct launch, rechecks the root and current selection, forwards no arguments and never falls back to an older release. `FullBundleVerified` remains false: other bundle files are not rehashed per launch. The production entry derives its root from its own executable directory and accepts no alternate-root flags.

Native fixtures compile and run the actual launcher against owned console peers, covering retained-release selection, tampering, malformed metadata, redirects, locks and selection changes. The same fixtures pass with an existing short-name TEMP alias after native canonicalization. Shortcuts, registration and launching the real installed application retain their integration and customer-acceptance gates.

`OwnedFiles` supplies the separate placement primitive. It publishes approved bytes without overwriting a path, and replaces or removes an existing file only when its descriptor still matches the root identity, file identity, length and hash. Changed, unrecorded, linked or redirected files stay in place. An interrupted replacement reports its retained previous bytes; a mapped previous executable may also remain in a reported backup. Native fixtures cover these outcomes with explicit peer readiness and terminal acknowledgement. Root pinning and checks retain cooperative limits against ancestor changes by the same user. Postinstall orchestration remains separate.

`SetupOwnership` records those descriptors in a bounded, strict journal bound to the engine installation ID and root identity. Foreign, malformed, linked or redirected journals are kept. Every save, including an identical save, checks the currently observed journal identity and bytes through ownership-aware placement and fences the installation record before and after. Saved descriptors record past placement; they do not prove that a file remains intact. Native fixtures cover round trips, concurrent edits, changed selections and interrupted publication. Postinstall integration, shortcuts and registration retain their own gates.

`ArcaneShellLink` creates and reads bounded shortcut bytes through in-memory Windows COM streams. The fixed fields select the canonical launcher, installation working directory and icon, with empty arguments. Inspection reports fields without resolving or starting a target; matching fields grant no target ownership or integrity. Native fixtures cover actual serialization, malformed bytes and unsafe target paths. Start Menu placement remains separate.

`InstallationActivity` provides a separate read-only Restart Manager snapshot for up to three caller-owned canonical files. A single count-only query reports Idle, Busy or Unknown without fetching process identities or terminating anything. Owned native peers cover running images, held ordinary files and acknowledged exits. Idle proves neither ownership nor safe removal; the future uninstall workflow must preserve its own identity and operation fences. Other sessions, elevated applications, services and DLL loads remain unverified.

Setup compiles and embeds a separate stable launcher with its size and SHA-256 pin. After a confirmed successful engine outcome, `PostInstall` checks the matching installation and selected release, validates the ownership journal, places only approved launcher bytes and records their descriptor. Partial recording never grants readiness or automatic adoption. Launcher replacement preserves the uninstaller descriptor. The setup window offers Open Arcane only after confirmed placement and journaling; that separate human action re-verifies the current selected executable without executing a mutable root stub. Native fixtures cover completion, refusal reasons, manual files, interrupted recording, replacement, resource pins and changed-installation launch refusals. The actual fixed-target GUI workflow remains unaccepted.

The separate application rebuild from SSH-signed source `133fb011c2d2cbf52f77c0a9663f43df918ba382` packages 4,186 files with manifest SHA-256 `d64e0dc1ec1cbbcc30c9193e41a66c35c8dd0b08190863e7427b23dd7c51c723`. All 32 actual executable checks passed, 24 critical files matched the isolated build and the workspace screenshot was reviewed. This rebuild has not yet been accepted through setup; the earlier component-composition receipt above still contains application source `186787684c1b964ea03c02d10c00c474889dcb5a` and predates launcher placement.
